newsitem.title: FRANCE: French minister wants EU anti-corruption drive.
newsitem.headline: French minister wants EU anti-corruption drive.

text.p: New French Justice Minister Elisabeth Guigou called in an interview released on Saturday for closer European cooperation to fight corruption, including direct cross-border links between investigation magistrates.
Guigou, a Socialist, told Le Journal du Dimanche reinforcing judicial cooperation among European states would be among her top priorities.

Among other goals she cited making public prosecutors independent of government interference, protecting the rights of the accused, reducing the prison population, protecting children and fighting racism and xenophobia.
"My priority...is also reinforcing European judicial cooperation to fight international corruption effectively.

"In this area, we must facilitate the indispensable direct relations between judges, while preserving the necessary safeguard clause when the higher national interests are at stake, as long as we do not have a federal (European) state," she said.

Guigou's comment contrasted with the action of her conservative predecessor, Jacques Toubon, who ordered magistrates to respect laborious diplomatic channels for passing on requests for judicial assistance in corruption cases, causing long delays in political sleaze investigations.

A group of corruption-fighting judges from France, Italy, Switzerland, Belgium and Spain launched an appeal earlier this year for politicians to lift the bureaucratic barriers to the European fight against white-collar crime and money-laundering.

By pointing to the safeguard clause, Guigou seemed to leave herself an escape clause, for example in dealing with Belgium's request for France to hand over documents on alleged bribery by planemaker Dassault Aviation of Belgian politicians.

The French minister is examining a pressing request from her Belgian counterpart to hand over 11 documents seized by French police in Belgium's investigation into Serge Dassault, chairman of the French aerospace company founded by his father.
